_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Bantu Settlement and Iron Age
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking peoples migrate into the Congo Basin; ironworking and agriculture replace hunter-gatherer economies; BaTwa (Pygmy) peoples remain in the forests.

910.name: Bantu Migration into the Congo Basin
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking farmers from the Cameroon-Nigeria borderland migrate southward and eastward through the equatorial forest; yam and oil-palm cultivation.

910.name: Iron Age Communities
910.label: Event
910.description: Iron smelting sites in the Niari Valley and Pool Malebo region; development of trade networks along the Congo River system.

920.name: Kongo Kingdom (Northern Territories)
920.label: Event
920.description: The Kongo Kingdom's northern provinces extend into modern Congo-Brazzaville; trade, Christianity, and political organisation shape the region.

920.name: Kongo Northern Provinces
920.label: Event
920.description: Provinces of Nsundi and Mpangu extend Kongo influence north of the Congo River; trade in copper, raffia cloth, and nzimbu shells.

920.name: Kongo Christianity and Portuguese Contact
920.label: Event
920.description: Kongo Kingdom adopts Christianity after Portuguese contact 1491; Afonso I's Christian kingdom; syncretic religious practices spread northward.

920.name: Teke (Tio) Kingdom
920.label: Event
920.description: The Teke Kingdom controls trade at Pool Malebo (Stanley Pool); mediates between coast and interior; the Makoko's authority shapes the region.

920.name: Teke Control of Pool Malebo Trade
920.label: Event
920.description: Teke (Tio/Anziku) kingdom controls strategic Pool Malebo portage; monopolises ivory and slave trade between coast and upper Congo.

920.name: Loango Kingdom and Coastal Trade
920.label: Event
920.description: Loango Kingdom on the Atlantic coast (Pointe-Noire region); independent of Kongo; major slave-trading port; Dutch and French commerce.

930.name: Atlantic Slave Trade and Coastal Commerce
930.label: Event
930.description: The Loango coast becomes a major slave-exporting region; internal wars fuel captive supply; European factories dot the littoral.

930.name: Loango Coast Slave Trade
930.label: Event
930.description: Loango, Malemba, and Cabinda ports export hundreds of thousands of enslaved people; Dutch, French, and Portuguese traders compete; trade transforms local societies.

930.name: Pierre de Brazza and the Makoko Treaty
930.label: Event
930.description: Italian-French explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signs a treaty with Teke king Makoko Iloo I 1880; establishes French claim to the north bank of the Congo.

940.name: French Congo and AEF (1882–1960)
940.label: Event
940.description: Brazzaville becomes capital of French Equatorial Africa; concessionary companies, forced labour, and the deadly Congo-Ocean Railway construction.

940.name: Concessionary Companies and Exploitation
940.label: Event
940.description: Vast concessions granted to private companies for rubber and ivory; André Gide's Voyage au Congo (1927) exposes abuses; international scandal.

940.name: Congo-Ocean Railway (CFCO)
940.label: Event
940.description: Construction of the Congo-Océan railway from Brazzaville to Pointe-Noire; estimated 17,000–23,000 forced labourers die; one of colonial Africa's worst atrocities.

950.name: Independence and Early Republic
950.label: Event
950.description: Fulbert Youlou leads independence; overthrown by trade unions 1963; Massamba-Débat introduces African socialism.

950.name: Abbé Youlou and Independence
950.label: Event
950.description: Abbé Fulbert Youlou becomes first president; Congo independent 15 August 1960; authoritarian rule; 'Trois Glorieuses' uprising topples him 1963.

950.name: Massamba-Débat and African Socialism
950.label: Event
950.description: Alphonse Massamba-Débat introduces MNR single-party socialism; youth militia; relations with Cuba and China; ousted by military 1968.

950.name: Marxist-Leninist People's Republic
950.label: Event
950.description: Marien Ngouabi declares People's Republic of Congo; PCT (Parti Congolais du Travail) Marxist-Leninist one-party state; assassinations and coups.

950.name: Ngouabi and the PCT
950.label: Event
950.description: Captain Marien Ngouabi establishes Marxist-Leninist state; renames country People's Republic of Congo; assassinated March 1977.

950.name: Sassou-Nguesso First Term
950.label: Event
950.description: Denis Sassou-Nguesso takes power 1979; maintains Marxist label but cultivates French and oil company ties; agrees to multiparty transition 1991.

960.name: Democratic Transition and Civil Wars
960.label: Event
960.description: National conference; Lissouba elected 1992; militia-based civil wars (1993, 1997, 1998–99); Sassou-Nguesso returns to power by force.

960.name: Lissouba Presidency and Political Crisis
960.label: Event
960.description: Pascal Lissouba wins multiparty election 1992; ethnic militias (Cocoyes, Cobras, Ninjas) form; political violence escalates.

960.name: Civil Wars (1997–1999)
960.label: Event
960.description: Sassou-Nguesso's Cobra militia and Angolan forces seize Brazzaville June–October 1997; second war 1998–99 devastates Pool region; tens of thousands killed.

960.name: Sassou-Nguesso and the Petro-State
960.label: Event
960.description: Sassou-Nguesso consolidates authoritarian rule; oil revenues fund patronage; constitutional amendments; international corruption investigations.

960.name: Sassou-Nguesso's Authoritarian Consolidation
960.label: Event
960.description: Post-war reconstruction; new constitution 2002; Pool region pacification; opposition marginalised; term limit removed 2015 via referendum.

960.name: Oil Economy and Corruption
960.label: Event
960.description: Congo becomes sub-Saharan Africa's third-largest oil producer; oil funds presidential patronage; 'biens mal acquis' French corruption investigations target Sassou family.
